name: Malaysia
headline: Malaysia: +5.2% growth in 2025, 1.4% inflation, debt 71% of GDP
sections: Malaysia is a $473 billion economy (2025), the world's 35th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.2% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $41K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 22.1% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 1.4% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 3.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 12.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 71% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −3.5% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +1.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 136% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 4.6% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 65% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.8 years (2024). Population: 33.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
